facts.statement: Gannansaurus was first named by Lü Junchang, Yi Laiping, Zhong Hui, and Wei Xuefang in 2013.
facts.quote: Gannansaurus was first named by Lü Junchang, Yi Laiping, Zhong Hui and Wei Xuefang in 2013

facts.statement: Most of the original specimen was destroyed during construction, but one dorsal vertebra was reconstructed from fragments.
facts.quote: Most of the specimen was destroyed as a result of the construction work, but one dorsal vertebra was able to be pieced back together from fragments.

facts.statement: The two preserved vertebrae are stored at the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History with the catalog number GMNH F10001.
facts.quote: The two vertebrae are stored at the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History with the catalog number GMNH F10001.

facts.statement: Gannansaurus lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, approximately between 72 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, hace aproximadamente entre 72 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Gannansaurus is more closely related to Euhelopus than to other titanosauriforms based on shared characters.
facts.quote: Gannansaurus shares some characters with Euhelopus, indicating that it is more closely related to it rather than to other titanosauriforms.

facts.statement: A 2023 phylogenetic analysis recovered Gannansaurus as a basal titanosauriform.
facts.quote: Gannansaurus was included in a phylogenetic analysis by Mo and colleagues in 2023, and was recovered as a basal titanosauriform.

facts.statement: Gannansaurus has been estimated to reach a length of 25 meters.
facts.quote: Gannansaurus has been estimated at 25 m long.

facts.statement: The time range for Gannansaurus is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gannansaurus belongs to the unranked family Somphospondyli.
